obtained.how: the authors' institutional copy: the University of Bergen theoretical-ecology group's papers directory (Aksnes's group), the typeset Sarsia article, 11 printed pages (pp. 137–147); equations read on the page image (PDF p. 3) because the text layer garbles them

bibliography.checked_against: the article's first page (PDF p. 1) and Crossref
bibliography.note: authors (Dag L. Aksnes & Anne Christine W. Utne), year, title, Sarsia 82: 137–147 all match; the issue number (2) is Crossref's, not printed on the article, which is dated 1997 08 15 (ISSN 0036-4827, Bergen). printed page = PDF page + 136

claims.claim: the reaction distance RD is scaled by prey size through R²e^(cR) ∝ prey area (the visual model R²·e^(cR) ∝ the prey's area)
claims.location: p. 139 (PDF p. 3), eq. 8 (from eqs. 3, 6–7); Table 1, p. 138 (PDF p. 2)
claims.quote: predicts the visual range (r) for a given target (C0,Ap) and given environmental conditions (Eb,c)
claims.conditions: eq. 8 reads r²·exp(cr) = |C0|·Ap·E′·Eb/(Ke + Eb), r the visual range (m), c the beam attenuation coefficient (m⁻¹), Ap the prey's area (m²), C0 its inherent contrast, E′ and Ke the eye's sensitivity and saturation parameters, Eb the background irradiance; so r²e^(cr) ∝ Ap only with contrast, eye and light held fixed. Fitted to a marine planktivorous goby, Gobiusculus flavescens, reacting to two copepods in the laboratory (Utne 1997: a light series, and turbidity series from diatomaceous earth at 12 and 120 µE m⁻² s⁻¹; Ke 4–5 µE m⁻² s⁻¹) and checked on goldfish and cod contrast thresholds
claims.note: two caveats for the text: (1) the model gives the VISUAL RANGE, which the authors take to exceed the reactive distance (they set the observed visual range r0 = mean reactive distance + 2 s.d., p. 139); scaling a piscivore's reaction distance by it assumes the two are proportional; (2) it was built and tested for planktivores and contrast-threshold data, not piscivores. The code (fish3.js:995) solves R²e^(cR) = R0²e^(cR0)·(L/6 cm)², i.e. eq. 8 with C0, E′ and light fixed

claims.claim: c = 1.7 m⁻¹ in the stained water (given inside the Aksnes & Utne citation)
claims.note: not in the source: Aksnes & Utne define c as the beam attenuation coefficient but give no value for any lake (their c values come from the transmission of diatomaceous-earth suspensions, pp. 139–140). 1.7 m⁻¹ is the project's estimate (fish3.js RD_C: Kd ≈ 0.85 m⁻¹ with c taken between K and 3K for humic water; realtime_foraging.md §5.3, after Fiksen et al. 2002 and Kirk 1980). Write it as "(Aksnes & Utne 1997), with c = 1.7 m⁻¹ for the stained water (project estimate)"

claims.claim: a visual reaction distance for every prey (R²·e^(cR) ∝ L²; Aksnes & Utne 1997)
claims.quote: linear response to increase in prey size (measured as length rather than area)
claims.conditions: p. 145 compares the model with the empirical reaction-distance models for bluegill, white crappie and alewife: "Our model behave in many respect similarly to their models", including this linear response to prey length; eq. 8 itself is in prey AREA
claims.note: ∝ L² is the project's step from area to length (prey of similar shape, area ∝ L²); the source's own variable is area. With c·R ≪ 1 the model reduces to R ∝ L, the empirical linear relation; the exp(cR) term flattens it at long range in turbid or stained water

notes: The model is cited correctly: R²e^(cR) ∝ prey area is the paper's eq. 8 with everything else fixed. The one fix is to mark c = 1.7 m⁻¹ as the project's estimate, and it is worth saying that the relation is for visual range and was fitted to a planktivorous goby. The §4.5 "follow-on mention" that show.mjs lists (the young-of-year paragraph) names Sørnes & Aksnes 2004, a different source; nothing there comes from Aksnes & Utne. Also in the source: eq. 9 fits T1 = Ap|C0|E′ = 7.5 × 10⁻² (Calanus) and 11.6 × 10⁻² (Acartia) with Ke = 5 µE m⁻² s⁻¹ (p. 141); with the light term Eb/(Ke + Eb), visual range rises fast at low light and is then "practically constant" as light increases further (p. 141, Fig. 2) — a ready mechanism if the model's light scaling of RD should follow the same equation; the formula in the project note (quoted there from Fiksen et al. 2002, eq. 2) has the same form as eq. 8.
